newsitem.title: USA: SangStat says Thymoglobulin test succeeds.
newsitem.headline: SangStat says Thymoglobulin test succeeds.

text.p: SangStat Medical Corp said on Monday a pivotal trial of its Thymoglobulin organ transplant drug was successful.
Based on the trial results, the company said it expects to file for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of the drug by the end of the year.
In the trial, which included 163 patients, Thymoglobulin had a success rate of 87.8 percent in reversing acute kidney graft rejection, the company said.
This compares with a 76.3 percent rate for Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc's ATGAM drug, SangStat said.
"The trial clearly demonstrates double-digit higher success rate for Thymoglobulin" versus ATGAM, SangStat Chief Executive Philippe Pouletty said in an interview.
UBS Securities analyst Marc Ostro said he expected Thymoglobulin could be on the U.S. market by the end of 1997.

Sangstat said last week that it expected to file for marketing clearance for its generic Cyclosporine. It said pivotal trials of the generic formulation showed it to be bioequivalent to other forms of branded cyclosorine now on the market.
